scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9103: A user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they have completely
lost connectivity to the partner network -- they cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) in
the peer AS since this morning. The team is convinced someone fat-fingered the
BGP configuration overnight and want the BGP config rolled back. Please find and
confirm the real fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: administratively down the inter-AS interface (eth0) on router1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is the inter-AS link: router1's eth0 (the interface to router2)
is DOWN, so the physical/L2 path between the two ASes is broken. As a CONSEQUENCE
the eBGP session between router1 and router2 drops and the inter-AS prefixes are
withdrawn, so pc1 (195.11.14.2) cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2). The ticket
MISDESCRIBES the cause as a BGP configuration error, but the BGP configuration is
intact and unchanged -- the session is down purely because the underlying link is
down, not because of any config mistake.

The correct diagnosis identifies router1 (inter-AS link / eth0 down) as the root
cause and explicitly notes the BGP loss is a downstream EFFECT, not the cause: the
BGP configuration on router1 and router2 is unchanged, so the user's "someone
broke the BGP config" hypothesis is wrong. An agent that rolls back / blames the
BGP configuration has accepted the ticket's misdescription instead of testing it.
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring the inter-AS link back up: on router1 run `ip link set eth0 up`. Once eth0
is up again, the eBGP session to router2 re-establishes, the inter-AS prefixes are
re-exchanged, and pc1 reaches pc2 normally. The BGP configuration needs no change
-- it was never modified.
scoring_axes: must-identify-link-down: identifies the inter-AS link (router1 eth0) is down as the root cause, with BGP loss as a consequence
bonus-rules-out-bgp-config: notes the BGP configuration is intact/unchanged, rejecting the "misconfigured BGP" cause

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on router1's eth0 interface (193.10.11.1/24), which connects to
router2 over the eBGP inter-AS link. Although the startup script correctly
assigns the IP address to eth0 via `ip address add 193.10.11.1/24 dev eth0`,
it is missing the companion command `ip link set eth0 up`. Linux interfaces
are administratively DOWN by default, so eth0 has been in a perpetual DOWN
state since the container started — confirmed by FRR reporting "Link ups: 0,
last: (never)" on that interface.

With eth0 down, the kernel never installs the 193.10.11.0/24 connected route,
making router1's BGP neighbor (193.10.11.2 on router2) completely unreachable
at the TCP layer. BGP on router1 is stuck in the Active state (unable to open
a session), while router2 shows a stale session from a prior state. Because no
BGP session is established from router1's perspective, router1 learns no route
to 200.1.1.0/24. When pc1 sends traffic to pc2 (200.1.1.2), router1 drops it
and returns "Destination Net Unreachable" — exactly the symptom reported.

The BGP configuration itself (AS numbers, neighbor IPs, advertised prefixes) is
correct on both routers and does not need to be rolled back. The sole root cause
is the missing `ip link set eth0 up` line in router1's startup script.

Corrective fix: On router1, run `ip link set eth0 up`. This will bring eth0 up,
install the 193.10.11.0/24 connected route, allow the BGP TCP session to
establish, and let router1 learn and propagate the 200.1.1.0/24 prefix,
restoring full pc1↔pc2 connectivity. The startup script should also be updated
to include this command permanently.
